tex_content.html:
Corollary
[Symmetry of cut points] ↗ prop:dc-ch13-2-2 1. ch13:2.7If $q$ is a cut point of $p$ along $\gamma $, then $p$ is the cut point of $q$ along $-\gamma $; in particular $q\in C_m(p)$ if and only if $p\in C_m(q)$.
Proof

\sketch By section 1, either $q$ is conjugate to $p$, or there is a geodesic $\sigma \neq \gamma $ from $p$ to $q$ with $\ell (\sigma )=\ell (\gamma )=d(p,q)$. In both cases the cut point of $q$ along $-\gamma $ does not occur before $p$; since $\ell (-\gamma )=d(p,q)$, $p$ is that cut point.

□
